newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 10.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* A group of investors led by Starwood Capital and Goldman Sachs is putting Westin Hotels up for sale, and possible bidders include Marriott International and a real estate investment trust that Starwood controls. The owners may also sell the hotel chain to the public through a stock offering.
* H.J. Heinz is expected to take a pretax charge of more than $500 million for a restructuring that would cut its work force by 6 percent.
* U.S. satellite companies are preparing for an auction of systems by Mexico that could bring in $1 billion.
* The U.S. Labor Department said payrolls grew by 339,000 in February, but hourly wages increased just 0.2 percent.
* Major airlines increased their domestic fares by 4 percent after a revived tax on air travel took effect Friday.
* The board of Conrail formally approved a $10.5 billion takeover by CSX, which will now focus on negotiations to divide Conrail's lines with Norfolk Southern .
* Ronald Perelman withdrew his competing reorganization plan for Marvel Entertainment and agreed to hand over the company to a group of bondholders led by Carl Icahn.
* Cablevision will control much of the New York sports market with its proposed purchase of Madison Square Garden, the New York Knicks and the New York Rangers from ITT Corp.
* Officers, directors and a former outside accountant for Leslie Fay have agreed to pay $34.7 million to settle a shareholder class action suit.
* Hewlett-Packard is expected to present software that will let technicians access personal computers over a network rather than in person.
* The Dow industrials rose 56.19 to 7,000.89, while bond prices rose and the dollar ended mixed.
* Regulators approved rules strengthening the investment practices of corporate credit unions.
* A federal appeals court has ruled that Lloyd's of London can be sued by American members for alleged fraud in the U.S.
* CMG is starting a service linking Internet access providers in a pool for advetisers wishing to reach their subscribers.
* Behind the fuss over Eli Lilly's new antipsychotic drug, Zyprexa, is a classic tale of how the slightest question can spur a run on even a large stock. --Heard on the Street.
* Don't look so smug, bond investors. Alan Greenspan was talking to you, too.
While exuberant stock investors seem to be taking a lot of heat from the chairman of the Federal Reserve these days, Mr, Greenspan had sharp words for the bond market as well. --Credit markets.
